chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Habash ibn Quniyy, who said: Ali ibn Sulayman al-Razi narrated to us from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Khaybari, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Qummi, who said:

He (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Whoever visits the grave of my father in Baghdad is like the one who visits the grave of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and the grave of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), except that the Messenger of Allah and the Commander of the Faithful have their own distinct superiority.'

key_terms.أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: The Commander of the Faithful (Imam Ali)
key_terms.قَبْرَ أَبِي: The grave of my father (referring to Imam al-Husayn)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting the grave of Imam al-Husayn in Baghdad?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the elevated spiritual status of the Qasim ibn Hasan shrine in Baghdad, often referred to as the 'Grave of the Imam' (Qabr al-Imam). Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) equates the reward of visiting this site to that of visiting the Prophet and Imam Ali, while explicitly preserving the unique, superior rank of the Prophet and the Commander of the Faithful. This comparison underscores the significance of the Abbasid Imams' burial sites in Shia devotional geography and jurisprudence.
